title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure: a synthetic video presented itself as the reporting of an established news outlet, and the false claim it carried was attributed to that outlet rather than to an anonymous source. The impersonation was the delivery mechanism, and the fabricated payment and the fabricated hacked emails were the payload. The video was distributed through a social platform account, not through any channel the outlet controlled, so the outlet's own editorial checks had no opportunity to intercept it.

The detection gap sits at the platform. The account that carried the video was created years earlier, had no followers, and behaved in a way consistent with automation, and the post accumulated a large view count within a day before any action was taken. The outlet's complaint was resolved as a trademark violation, which addresses the misuse of a brand rather than the falsity of the claim. Catching this before wide distribution would have required the platform to weigh account provenance and posting behaviour against the apparent authority of the outlet being imitated.

What is not established is who exactly operated the account, whether the network's intent can be proven from a single post, and how much of the audience believed the video rather than merely saw it. The attribution to a named network rests on researchers and the reporting outlet, and the claim that the campaign has not yet achieved significant reach is the reporters' assessment at the time of publication.

reports.title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

summary:
A Russian disinformation network known as Storm-1679 or Matryoshka circulated a fake video falsely branded as Mother Jones reporting. The video claimed the Democratic National Committee paid $259 million to CNN head Mark Thompson to promote gender transition among children, citing emails supposedly hacked by Anonymous. It was posted on X by an account called роман, a likely bot created in 2018 with no followers, and drew 155,000 views within a day, plus 50,000 more from another account. The video was fake, and Mother Jones complained to X, which removed the post for a trademark violation.

The network has spread similar deepfakes, including fake CNN reports and videos of celebrities such as Sarah Jessica Parker urging votes for Republicans, plus false stories about Democratic Senate candidates. Researchers say the current campaign has not gained much reach yet, but in 2024 Matryoshka content reached millions of Americans. The article says the Trump administration has closed FBI, intelligence, and State Department units that tracked foreign disinformation, leaving the US less able to counter Russian operations ahead of the midterms.
title_en: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake
